reasons: The cited text supports the deviation: Section 15.2 contains only Effective-Date reps (IP ownership, no conflicting grants, litigation, legal compliance) and Article IX defers specifications and 'customary terms' to future supply agreements, so no conformance warranty or remedy for Materials exists under this Agreement — squarely the rule's 'missing express warranty is a deviation (insert)' case, and below the fallback (no remedy at all).

The rationale correctly notes that 15.4's disclaimer carves out express terms, so the issue is the absence of an express warranty rather than a disclaimer that swallows it — this avoids mischaracterizing the clause.

The inserted Section 9.7 is actionable and directionally correct for the customer: conformance to specifications/CoA, GMP and applicable Law, professional and workmanlike performance, and replacement or refund at Ono's election — matching the preferred position's warranty-plus-remedy structure without rewriting existing text.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing variant, not a substantive gap: tying conformance to delivery plus shelf life/retest date is the industry-standard formulation for pharmaceutical Materials and is at least as protective as a 90-day window; the comment also offers a shorter window as a fallback.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, prefixed, accurately describes the change and the playbook basis, and offers a sensible fallback. Minor points only (not disqualifying): the new section is numbered 9.7 immediately after 9.6(b) and should be checked against existing Article IX numbering, and the addition of shipping/handling/destruction costs goes slightly beyond the model remedy language.
